title: OKC: Finals Game 1, 2012
description: A 13-point hole, 36 in the fourth-quarter takeover, and a near triple-double—Go Deep into the night OKC took Game 1 of the 2012 Finals.
imageHint: Chesapeake Energy Arena, June 2012, blue and orange roaring

questions.question: In Game 1 of the 2012 NBA Finals, which Thunder star scored 36 points—including 17 in the fourth—to beat Miami?
questions.explanation: Twelve-of-twenty from the field at home. Once OKC took the lead late in the third, it never trailed again.

questions.question: Durant's running mate that night nearly had a triple-double with 27 points, 11 assists, and 8 boards—who?
questions.explanation: Westbrook's second-half aggression flipped the game. Three of Durant's late buckets came directly off his dimes.

questions.question: Westbrook's layup-and-one with 16.4 seconds left in the third gave OKC the lead for good against which LeBron–Wade–Bosh franchise?
questions.explanation: LeBron finished with 30. It wasn't enough. Final: Thunder 105, Heat 94—OKC's first Finals win as a franchise.

questions.question: After that 105–94 Game 1, Miami won the series. How many games did the Heat win in the Finals?
questions.explanation: Heat took Games 2 through 5 for a 4–1 series. Game 1 remains the what-if night—the loudest Chesapeake ever got in June.

questions.question: In that Game 1 win, which Thunder big came off the bench for 10 rebounds and helped own the glass 43–35?
questions.explanation: Collison's offensive boards fueled the fourth-quarter run. Perkins started; the glue guy cleaned up. Locals still cheer the name.

questions.question: In what year did the Seattle SuperSonics relocate and become the Oklahoma City Thunder?
questions.hint: Clay Bennett, bitter arena fight, Sam Presti already GM

questions.question: Durant was the last SuperSonics draft pick—selected which overall in 2007?

easterEgg.title: One lead change
easterEgg.text: Box-score trivia from that Game 1: there was only one lead change the entire night. Once Westbrook put OKC ahead late in the third, the lead never flipped back.
